# About this book {.unnumbered}

**MoQ for the Curious** explains how Media over QUIC delivers live content: how publishers name it, relays distribute it, and players keep it useful when the network slows.

The book introduces networking and media concepts as they are needed. A live lecture provides a running example, from the first subscription to playback and debugging.

This book is inspired by [WebRTC for the Curious](https://webrtcforthecurious.com/) and its approach to explaining how the pieces of a real-time communication system fit together.

[Start reading: What, Why and How →](docs/01-what-why-and-how/index.qmd)

## Where to begin

The first chapter explains what MoQ is, why it is useful, and how five activities fit together: connect, discover, request, deliver, and present. It then shows [how MoQ compares with WebRTC](docs/01-what-why-and-how/index.qmd#how-does-moq-compare-with-webrtc) and maps those activities to the chapters ahead. Tracks, groups, and objects give those steps a shared vocabulary. The later chapters cover security, a first experiment, and debugging.

A fictional lecture runs through the examples. When a new term appears, we explain what it means and why it matters. The [glossary](docs/12-glossary/index.qmd) is here whenever a word gets in the way.

## A protocol still taking shape

This edition uses **MOQT draft-21**, published September 8, 2026, as its IETF baseline. Implementation examples are labeled separately from protocol requirements.

Initial research was completed on **September 16, 2026**, with a technical fact-check on **September 22, 2026**. Each chapter links to primary sources; the [references](docs/13-references/index.qmd) explain the source policy and limitations. Example latency values are teaching aids, not benchmarks, and the upstream walkthrough commands have not been executed for this guide.

## Maintenance and contributions

This book is maintained by [@pham-tuan-binh](https://github.com/pham-tuan-binh). Corrections, clearer explanations, and new examples are welcome. The [GitHub repository and contribution guide](https://github.com/pham-tuan-binh/moq-for-the-curious#readme) explain how to edit and build the book. You can submit a pull request directly, or email [binhpham@binhph.am](mailto:binhpham@binhph.am) to suggest a change or ask for an update.
